definitions.definition: (revenue - cost of goods sold - SG&A - interest expense) / book equity, fiscal year t-1, formed each June
definitions.gap: Operating income already deducts COGS and SG&A, but interest expense is not deducted (no interest-expense field in the PIT store); TTM rather than fiscal-year t-1; refreshed per filing rather than each June.

definitions.definition: (revenue - cost of goods sold) / total assets
definitions.gap: Neither store collects cost of goods sold or gross profit (US FLOWS and KR WANTED_ACCOUNTS list revenue, operating income, net income, equity, liabilities, assets, operating cash flow, capex). Operating income also deducts SG&A, which Novy-Marx deliberately does not; this is a different measure (closer to operating profitability / assets), not a weaker version of GP/A.

definitions.definition: net income (TTM) / book equity among large caps with operating margin > 0 and liabilities/equity <= 2
definitions.gap: Bottom-line and levered: includes interest, taxes, non-operating and one-off items, and rises with leverage (the <= 2 cap limits but does not remove that). It is an in-house proxy motivated by the profitability literature, NOT a reproduction of either academic strategy.

levels.E0: HYPOTHESIS — an economic story or an AI hypothesis; no return evidence
levels.E1: EXTERNALLY_DOCUMENTED — independent academic/empirical evidence read from a primary page or abstract; not reproduced here
levels.E2: LOCALLY_REPLICATED — passes PIT and basic economics on our market, data and horizon under pre-fixed conditions
levels.E3: ROBUSTNESS_SUPPORTED — survives other start dates, periods, industries, costs, risk exposures and an independent window
levels.E4: PROSPECTIVE_OBSERVED — economics evaluated on records published before the decision, with enough horizon and power
levels.E5: DEPLOYMENT_ELIGIBLE — pre-set source, statistical, economic and operational conditions met, plus a separate Owner approval

literature.sourcePolicy: Only what was read on the page listed is stated as the source's claim. Full texts behind paywalls (Wiley, Springer, SSRN) were not read; their abstracts were read via RePEc/IDEAS or NBER.

applicability.KR: Not covered by the library; Korea has no comparable survivorship-free public dataset in this repository.
applicability.US: Directly measurable: the library's long-only sorted portfolios are survivorship-free (CRSP) and lagged; used for the academic-path test.

studies.citation: Fama & French (2015), five-factor model; Ken French Data Library 'Fama/French 5 Factors (2x3)'
studies.method: Six value-weight 2x3 portfolios on size and B/M, size and operating profitability (OP), size and investment; formed end of June with accounting data for the fiscal year ending in t-1; NYSE breakpoints; all NYSE, AMEX and NASDAQ stocks. RMW = 1/2 (Small Robust + Big Robust) - 1/2 (Small Weak + Big Weak); HML and CMA analogous. Monthly data from July 1963.
studies.originalStructure: long-short, value-weighted, broadly diversified, annual rebalancing
studies.overlapWithOurSignals: value sleeve (B/P), quality sleeve (roe, margins, leverage) approximate HML and RMW; our sleeves are percentile composites, not 2x3 sorts

applicability.KR: Already tested: momentum and industry momentum in KR ML tournaments; industry momentum is rebalance-phase dependent.
applicability.US: Momentum is already in production's momentum sleeve; local rank IC -0.0015 (p 0.92). The library's big-winner portfolio is reported here as descriptive only.

studies.method: Strategies that buy past winners and sell past losers generate significant positive returns over three- to twelve-month holding periods; not explained by systematic risk or delayed reaction to common factors; part of the first-year abnormal return dissipates in the following two years (abstract).
studies.originalStructure: long-short winner/loser portfolios across many stocks (details beyond the abstract not read)
studies.overlapWithOurSignals: momentum sleeve (12-1 and 6-month returns), industry momentum rule, ML price features

applicability.KR: Same; KR quality coverage gaps (value/quality missing 54-55% in the attribution audit).
applicability.US: Our quality sleeve covers profitability and leverage (safety) only partially; growth and payout components are not built.

studies.citation: Asness, Frazzini & Pedersen (2019), Quality Minus Junk, Review of Accounting Studies 24(1)
studies.method: Quality = characteristics investors should pay more for: profitability, growth and safety. High-quality stocks have higher prices but not by much and earn high risk-adjusted returns; a QMJ factor (long quality, short junk) earns significant risk-adjusted returns in the US and across 24 countries; the price of quality varies over time and a low price predicts high future QMJ returns (abstract).
studies.originalStructure: long-short factor; component measures and breakpoints not read
studies.overlapWithOurSignals: quality sleeve; the four-factor attribution audit measured quality 126D rank IC -0.022 pooled

applicability.KR: DART gross profit coverage not built; not measurable.
applicability.US: Gross profits / assets is not derived in our PIT store (no gross profit or total-assets field); ROE and operating margin are the available proxies. The library's OP sorts are the closest public long-only test.

studies.citation: Novy-Marx (2013), The Other Side of Value: The Gross Profitability Premium, JFE 108(1) 1-28 (NBER w15940)
studies.method: Profitability measured by gross profits-to-assets has roughly the same power as book-to-market in predicting the cross-section of average returns; profitable firms earn higher returns despite lower book-to-market and larger size; controlling for profitability raises value strategy performance, especially among the largest, most liquid stocks (abstract).
studies.overlapWithOurSignals: quality sleeve, S2 value-confirmation (cheap AND confirmed by profit/cash flow)

applicability.both: Governs our rules: the B1 screen uses one signal, the academic-path test pre-registers one primary portfolio and a Bonferroni threshold, and no composite is fitted.

studies.citation: Novy-Marx (2015), Backtesting Strategies Based on Multiple Signals (NBER w21329)
studies.method: Strategies that combine multiple signals suffer severe overfitting bias because each signal is signed to predict positive in-sample returns; combinations of random signals can look highly significant; appropriate critical values can be several times standard levels; combining the best k of n signals is almost as biased as picking the best of n^k (abstract).
studies.overlapWithOurSignals: directly relevant to the four-factor composite, ML tournaments (141 models) and the cocktail policies

literature.timeSeriesVsCrossSection: All five are cross-sectional (which stocks beat others), not forecasts of the market index. Market-timing evidence (C1 exposure, US cocktail) is a separate question and is graded separately.

PRODUCTION.rule: the weights of the FINAL_WEEKLY production receipt of the decision date, copied by digest

b1Steps: universe: the census stage-3 survivors (common identity, tradable, 252 sessions of history, no unresolved corporate action)
inputs: the latest single filing, visible strictly before the decision date, that states ROE, operating margin, net margin and liabilities/equity, with a report period at most 456 days old
eligible: large cap (KR market-cap rank <= 150, US S&P 500), 0 < operating margin <= 1, liabilities/equity <= 2
rank by ROE (descending, ties by ticker); walk down the ranking and take a name unless its industry already holds 2 selected names; stop at 5
industry: KR = kr-industry-membership-foundation-v4 interval containing the decision date; US = pipeline.sectors.sector_of; an unknown industry is the shared bucket UNCLASSIFIED with the same cap

cohort.decisionDate: the asOfDate of the first FINAL_WEEKLY production receipt of the month in each region (KR and US separately)
cohort.execution: close of the first regional session whose open is at least 48 hours after the cohort packet is sealed; identical for all four arms
cohort.frequency: monthly, independent: each cohort is a separate buy-and-hold portfolio to its horizons; cohorts overlap and are never netted against each other
cohort.informationCutoff: the regional close of the decision date (KR 15:30 Asia/Seoul, US 16:00 America/New_York)
cohort.noBackfill: an arm that is not committed by the deadline is NO_RECORD for that cohort and is never filled in later
cohort.recordedAt: the commit time of the cohort file, verified public before the deadline by an observation made before the deadline (ledger PUBLICATION rule)
cohort.registrationDeadline: the open of the execution session

comparison.excludedFromPrimary: records annotated PIT_CONTAMINATED, PUBLICATION_LATE or PUBLICATION_NOT_OBSERVED; they stay in the ledger and are reported separately
comparison.noEarlyClaim: no statement about an arm's edge before 24 cohorts have matured at 126 sessions; until then outcomes are listed, not summarised
comparison.primary: per cohort and horizon: B1_ROE - ETF100, B1_PLUS_AI - B1_ROE (the AI's marginal effect), PRODUCTION - ETF100, after base costs

costs.basis: the production receipt's stated round-trip cost per leg (stock and ETF) on the decision date
costs.stress: 2x the same costs, reported beside the base case for every outcome

gates.detail: FRED values are read at the current vintage. An observation revised after the cutoff is dropped when revision metadata is supplied (availability.available_fred), but the FRED CSV carries none, so a silent revision cannot be detected. Prospective-v1 arms read no macro series.

Production receipts carry no per-field publication time. A stated time after the cutoff now fails gate G6_PUBLICATION; an absent one is flagged, not trusted. Prospective-v1 arms read dated PIT filings (availableFrom strictly before the decision date).

PUBLICATION_VERIFIED needs the public commit to be OBSERVED before the deadline; a later check can only record PUBLICATION_NOT_OBSERVED. An operator must therefore run verify-publication before each deadline.
Clarified: the registration deadline applies to every path. A cohort decided after it records nothing (REGISTRATION_CLOSED); no path is back-filled.

entry: a pre-registered hypothesis whose rule is in this file (rule SHA-256 recorded on every record)

the rule's own evidence grade is at least E1 and its evidence-grades item lists no block in prospectiveBlocks (a block on NEW HISTORICAL research, such as KR GOVERNANCE_CLOSED, does not stop a prospective record)

evidenceFirst.rule: Levels are sequential: an item's grade is the highest level whose criteria AND every lower level's criteria are met. A famous paper never skips a level. Blocking states (SOURCE_BLOCKED, PIT_UNSAFE, PIT_CONTAMINATED, GOVERNANCE_CLOSED) are listed separately and make an item ineligible for a decision whatever its grade.
evidenceFirst.survivorshipStatement: The US census lists today's members only. It supports a current screen, never a historical performance claim.

tracks.C_WATCHLIST_ONLY: everything else: may be shown and discussed, never recorded as a portfolio

reasons: A profitable, moderately levered insurer (ROE about 27%) priced below the index multiple
Near-zero equity beta and a shallow drawdown: it diversifies the 90% SPY residual while VIX is 28
The production entry layer is ACCUMULATE_GRADUALLY, and no frozen gate or contradicting layer applies
risks: A sharp equity rally: with beta near 0 it would lag SPY
A softening commercial P&C pricing cycle
The FCF yield includes insurance float and overstates distributable cash
picks.thesis12m: Over a year, the stock tracks underwriting profitability plus investment income on a book that reinvests at higher yields. At a below-market multiple it does not need multiple expansion to keep pace with SPY.
picks.thesis6m: If the US correction deepens or stays choppy (VIX near 28), a low-beta insurer earning high returns on equity should hold value better than SPY. The 10% sleeve should then add relative return.
picks.whyVersusBenchmark: Its return driver (underwriting plus investment income) is largely independent of SPY's growth-heavy driver. A 10% sleeve tests whether a profitable low-beta name can beat the index after costs, without betting the book.

reviewedRejected.reason: Risk layer contradicts. Cheapness on cyclical earnings is not evidence of mispricing without margin data.
Only 1 layer supports. The quality signal is an accounting artifact, the valuation basis (FFO) is missing, and the macro layer is adverse.
